newsitem.title: USA: DeKalb knows no reason for stock drop.
newsitem.headline: DeKalb knows no reason for stock drop.

text.p: DeKalb Genetics Corp said Monday it knew of no reason for a drop in its stock, which traded off 3-3/4 at 75 in the late morning.
"There's nothing that we are aware of," DeKalb Chief Financial Officer Thomas Rauman said.

Analysts also said they knew of no reason for the decline in the stock, other than heavier-than-normal volume for DeKalb, which is normally thinly traded. In the late morning, nearly 84,000 shares traded.
"The seed stocks have been rather volatile," added Piper Jaffray analyst George Dahlman.

Last week, Pioneer Hi-Bred International Inc shares traded lower after that company said its 1997 North American seed corn market share likely would be 42 to 42.5 percent, down one-and-a-half to two percentage points. That drop was larger than analysts had been expecting.
Pioneer shares in the late morning Monday were up 3/8 at 75-1/8.
